notes:
I couldn't do this research. My first attempt to open the commentary pages hit the tool's usage limit before any page loaded, so I have no content from any of the approved sites.

Your rules say to report only what the pages I read actually say, and I didn't read any. So I haven't written verse-by-verse notes. Writing them from my own memory and attaching URLs would make it look as if sources had been checked when they hadn't.

Ask again in a new message and I'll start with these pages:

- **Traditional verse-by-verse reading:** Enduring Word on Psalm 87; Gill, Ellicott, Barnes and the Pulpit Commentary on biblehub.com; preceptaustin.org.
- **Protestant traditions:** Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* (spurgeon.org or studylight.org); Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu); Reformed sources on ligonier.org and thegospelcoalition.org; Lutheran material on lcms.org and 1517.org.
- **Other views:** NET Bible notes for modern scholarship, especially on verse 4 (Rahab and Babylon) and verse 7 (the singers and pipers); Augustine's exposition on newadvent.org, where Psalm 87 is numbered Psalm 86; Orthodox material on oca.org.

Then I'll write the notes in the "v. 4: …" format with a URL after each point, and leave out anything I can't find.
